chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: 'A man whose intention is sincerity/trustworthiness, but when he measures he does not do so well.' He said: 'What do those around him say?' I said: 'They say he does not give full measure.' He said: 'It is not fitting for him to measure.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a merchant who intends to be honest but measures incorrectly?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between mere intention (*niyyah*) and practical competence in trade, ruling that a merchant who cannot measure accurately despite good intentions is unfit for the role. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and technical proficiency as prerequisites for valid commercial transactions, ensuring that honesty is not compromised by negligence. The ruling underscores that the social perception of fairness ('they say he does not fulfill') is intrinsically linked to the actual execution of the duty.
